ops.entry: WHEN check-state exits 1 on INV-26 at a review pin DO rerun it at the feature tip before reporting a defect — INV-26 reads the live GitHub board, so a pin predating a station-move commit shows a false projection mismatch.
ops.why: Measured this feature: INV-26 exited 1 at the pin and 0 at the tip, which differed only in feature-dir station records; recurs on every validate at a pin. G-11 (preserve output on discovery-count divergence) is generic hygiene and the weakest repo gotcha.

originals.original: WHEN run-unit-tests.py reports a different discovery-file count for the same --kind invocation DO preserve complete output and invocation environment; unreconciled discovery sets make a divergent exit unauditable.

ops.entry: WHEN a criterion's literal wording is stricter than what its assertion can see ('raw bytes' against a decoded or newline-normalized read) DO grade the gap against the letter, not present equivalence; run the mutant it admits and route text-unmet upward — today's equivalence is not what the test pins.
ops.why: Sharper successor to O-04: I followed its route-up step yet rated a raw-bytes letter miss low on measured present equivalence; the ruler judged it the one real clause miss (CRLF writer passed every row) and it cost a completion round.

ops.entry: WHEN a behaviour-delta probe finds a delta the signed decision covers literally but the signoff or plan characterizes otherwise DO report it as a finding for the ruler, naming the characterization it falsifies — classifying it in-class yourself pre-empts the stop-and-rule clause that falsified characterization triggers.
ops.why: I recorded a row-erasing fold as in-class; two reviewers escalated it and the ruler confirmed the signoff's 'bytes identical' was false, so the stop clause had fired. O-08 (mutate the real call site, not a passthrough accessor) is largely subsumed by O-06/O-10 and is the weakest Outcome.

originals.original: WHEN a criterion's literal wording is stricter than the artifact scoping it DO report two distinct findings — intent-satisfied and text-unmet — and route the verdict up, rather than recording the criterion as satisfied under your own reading.

WHEN crediting a test as evidence a per-key behavior is read from data rather than hardcoded DO confirm the tested function itself branches on that key — a key-agnostic passthrough (e.g. `dict[key]`) proves nothing about the real, revertable call site; mutate that call site directly instead of the accessor.
